title: Jio IPO Draws Rs 69,800 Crore in Bids on Day One, Subscribed 3.16 Times
excerpt: Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213-crore issue, India's largest ever, was fully subscribed in 100 minutes on October 21, led by institutional bids at 9.42 times the QIB quota, with retail at 0.73 times ahead of the October 23 close.
body:
• Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213-crore IPO was subscribed 3.16 times on day one, drawing bids worth about Rs 69,800 crore for 62.36 crore shares against 19.75 crore on offer.
  • The issue was fully subscribed within 100 minutes on October 21, which PTI reported as the fastest full subscription for a mega IPO in India, ahead of the first-day pace of the LIC, NSE and GIC issues.
  • Qualified institutional buyers led demand at 9.42 times their quota, while non-institutional investors subscribed 1.68 times, the shareholder portion 1.46 times and retail 0.73 times.
  • For investors still deciding: bidding closes Friday, October 23, the price band is Rs 1,065-1,119, one lot is 12 shares (Rs 13,428 at the upper band), and allotment is expected on October 26.

Jio Platforms drew bids worth about Rs 69,800 crore on the first day of its initial public offering, as India's largest-ever public issue was subscribed 3.16 times on Wednesday, according to The Economic Times, citing combined exchange data as of 7 pm. Investors bid for 623.6 million shares against 197.5 million shares on offer.

The Rs 30,213-crore issue, priced at Rs 1,065-1,119 per share, was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening. Taken together with anchor commitments secured earlier in the week, the offering had attracted about Rs 77,892 crore, PTI reported, with total demand reaching Rs 3.20 lakh crore once anchor bids were counted.

Institutions Drove Day One

Qualified institutional buyers bid for 461.5 million shares against 49 million reserved for them, a subscription of 9.42 times. Non-institutional investors bid 1.68 times their portion, the employee quota was subscribed 1.36 times and the portion reserved for Reliance Industries shareholders was subscribed 1.46 times, The Economic Times reported.

Retail investors bid for 61.7 million shares against 85 million reserved, or 0.73 times. Despite staying below full subscription on day one, PTI reported that the retail portion recorded the highest day-one retail demand for any IPO in India's capital market history, at about Rs 6,908 crore in the Flash Finance summary of the exchange figures. Retail bidding in large issues typically builds toward the final day.

On October 19, Jio Platforms raised about Rs 8,110 crore from 212 anchor investors at Rs 1,119 per share, the upper end of the band, after an anchor book that attracted bids exceeding Rs 2.5 lakh crore, more than 30 times the allocation, PTI reported. Investors named in that report included BlackRock, Fidelity Investments, GIC and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority.

How Day One Compares

According to Prime Database figures cited by The Economic Times, the Rs 11,605-crore LG Electronics IPO in October last year was the only other Indian public issue above Rs 10,000 crore to have been fully subscribed on its opening day. Other mega issues, including Tata Capital, Life Insurance Corporation of India, General Insurance Corporation of India and the National Stock Exchange of India, recorded lower first-day subscriptions.

PTI made the same point from the other direction: Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870-crore IPO, which held the previous record for India's largest public offering, was subscribed just 18 per cent by the end of its first day in 2024. Jio's issue is also structurally different. It is an entirely fresh issue of up to 27 crore new shares, with no offer for sale, so the proceeds go to the company rather than to selling shareholders.

Where the Money Goes

Jio Platforms is the digital and telecom arm of Reliance Industries, led by Mukesh Ambani. The company plans to use up to Rs 27,500 crore of the proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings of its subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm, with the balance earmarked for general corporate purposes, The Economic Times reported. At the upper end of the band the issue values Jio Platforms at about $108 billion, PTI reported.

Moody's said the IPO was credit positive for Reliance because proceeds would cut debt at Reliance Jio Infocomm, PTI reported. CreditSights expected Reliance's stake to fall to about 64.5 per cent from 66.4 per cent, retaining control.

What Happens Next

The issue remains open until Friday, October 23. Outlook Money, reporting the company's October 14 exchange filing, put the basis of allotment on October 26, while PTI reported listing scheduled for October 28. Eligible employees receive a discount of Rs 54 per share, and reservations of up to Rs 500 crore for employees and up to Rs 2,500 crore for eligible Reliance Industries shareholders apply, according to Outlook Money.

For diaspora investors, bidding requires an Indian demat account and an ASBA or UPI mandate completed before the October 23 close, and the shareholder quota is limited to eligible Reliance Industries shareholders as of October 14. Friday's final tally and the October 26 allotment will show whether retail demand caught up with institutions.
